advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_a_custom_workflow_status_set_reaches_the_probe_classifier exercise probe_remote (patch the transport's client to return a status-200 payload and assert the resulting branch reflects `custom`), so it verifies the transport actually threads _resolved_statuses into classify_probe_response rather than reading the stored attribute.
evidence: Docstring claim: 'Pinning this against the CLASSIFIER rather than the settings tuple is the point: a value that is stored but never consulted would satisfy a weaker assertion' (test file lines 132-134)

The classify_probe_response call uses the local `custom`, not the transport: `classify_probe_response("X-1", 200, {"fields": {"status": {"name": "Shipped"}}}, resolved_statuses=custom)` (lines 144-146)
The only transport assertion reads the stored attribute: `assert transport._resolved_statuses == custom` (line 148)

The real wiring the test purports to cover is probe_remote passing self._resolved_statuses: transport.py:313-317 `return classify_probe_response(remote_id, status_code/200, ..., resolved_statuses=self._resolved_statuses)` — never called by this test
Test docstring: "Pinning this against the CLASSIFIER rather than the settings tuple is the point: a value that is stored but never consulted would satisfy a weaker assertion" (lines 132-134)

The test never calls transport.probe_remote; it only reads `transport._resolved_statuses == custom` (line 148), a private attribute — a change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving rename with no observable change
transport.py:313-317: `classify_probe_response(remote_id, status_code, {}, resolved_statuses=self._resolved_statuses)` — this is the threading the test claims to pin, but it is never executed

The classify_probe_response call at lines 144-146 is fed `custom` by the test itself, so it verifies only that the pure classifier honors the set handed to it, not that the transport supplies its configured set
advisory.finding: test_a_custom_workflow_status_set_reaches_the_probe_classifier does not assert what its docstring claims: it calls classify_probe_response with a locally-constructed `custom` (not with the transport's stored set) and only asserts `transport._resolved_statuses == custom`, which is exactly the 'stored but never consulted' attribute check the docstring disparages. The transport->classifier wiring in probe_remote (self._resolved_statuses is passed to classify_probe_response) is never exercised, so a regression that stopped probe_remote from threading _resolved_statuses through would still pass this test.
merged_from: test_a_custom_workflow_status_set_reaches_the_probe_classifier does not exercise the transport's probe path (probe_remote) and asserts the config threading only via the private attribute transport._resolved_statuses; it therefore cannot detect a regression where probe_remote stops passing self._resolved_statuses to the classifier (transport.py:313-317), which is the exact behavior the test name and docstring claim to pin.
scenarios: A refactor of probe_remote that hardcodes DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES or drops the resolved_statuses argument would leave this test green while breaking DC absence classification for custom workflows.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the classifier assertion to `assert shipped.branch is ProbeBranch.PRESENT_RESOLVED` so it detects the case where the custom resolved-status vocabulary is not consulted.
evidence: probe.py:41-45: status 200 with status_name in resolved_statuses => PRESENT_RESOLVED; else => PRESENT_FILTERED — neither is UNREACHABLE
Assertion `shipped.branch is not ProbeBranch.UNREACHABLE` (line 147) passes for both PRESENT_RESOLVED and PRESENT_FILTERED
If the custom set were ignored (Shipped not treated as resolved), the result would be PRESENT_FILTERED — still not UNREACHABLE — so the assertion still passes
advisory.finding: The classifier assertion `assert shipped.branch is not ProbeBranch.UNREACHABLE` (line 147) is too weak: a 200 response whose status is NOT in resolved_statuses returns PRESENT_FILTERED, which is also not UNREACHABLE, so the assertion cannot distinguish 'Shipped classified as resolved' from 'Shipped ignored'.
scenarios: A regression where the custom vocabulary is dropped and 'Shipped' is not recognized as resolved still yields PRESENT_FILTERED, passing this assertion
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `assert shipped.branch is not ProbeBranch.UNREACHABLE` with `assert shipped.branch is ProbeBranch.PRESENT_RESOLVED`.
